findings.summary: Section numbers are duplicated and run out of sequence across the part, so the numbered progression a learner would follow is meaningless.
findings.evidence: Page 1: "2. Toolkit For Empty Images" → "3. Mounts Aren't Showing" → "2. Security Posture"; page 2: "4. Reproduce It Minimally" → "5. What Each Layer Costs" → "1. Storage Speed Truth" → "4. The Model, One Line"; page 3: "3. The Operational Trade" → "5. Six Lines To Keep"; page 4: "6. Back Up A Volume" → "7. DNS In One Box". Page 1 opens with an unnumbered bullets+table block, and "1" first appears midway through page 2.
findings.fix: Renumber every heading sequentially in reading order (1…N across pages 1-4), including a "1." heading for page 1's opening symptom bullets/table, or drop the numbers entirely.

findings.summary: The caption's first sentence is a bare part-number label rather than a hook, burying the actual hook in sentence two.
findings.evidence: "Part 2 of DOCKER NETWORKING & VOLUMES. Your container can't be reached and your database just vanished — same root cause: ..."
findings.fix: Lead with the hook and demote the part label: "Your container can't be reached and your database just vanished — same root cause: namespaces gave it a private network and a disposable filesystem. Part 2 of DOCKER NETWORKING & VOLUMES walks the whole path: ..."

findings.summary: The step declared as the first debugging action appears third on the page, buried under the netshoot toolkit heading.
findings.evidence: The page opens with loopback bullets, the symptom table and the MTU Q&A; only after "2. Toolkit For Empty Images" and the `nicolaka/netshoot` code block does the bullet "Step 1 always: `docker inspect c` — `.NetworkSettings`, `.Mounts`." appear.
findings.fix: Move the `docker inspect` / `docker port` / `ss -ltnp` / `tcpdump` bullets to the top of page 1 under their own heading, ahead of the symptom table, and leave only netshoot + nsenter under the toolkit heading.

findings.summary: The "Security Posture" code block ends the debugging page with hardening flags whose justification only arrives on pages 2 and 3.
findings.evidence: Page 1 ends with heading "2. Security Posture" and bare lines "--read-only --tmpfs /run" / "--cap-drop=ALL --user 1000:1000" with no prose; the reasons appear later — page 2: "Isolation is only as good as the process privileges." and page 3: "Daemon access is ==root on the host==, full stop."
findings.fix: Delete the security heading/code from page 1 and place that code with the security bullets on pages 2-3, so the flags and their rationale sit together.
Run the fit pass — it adds material from the book without removing anything.

findings.summary: `docker volume prune` no longer deletes all unreferenced volumes by default — since Docker 23.0 (API 1.42) it removes only anonymous volumes unless `--all` is passed.
findings.fix: Change the Deletes cell to "unused anonymous volumes; add `-a/--all` for named ones" (and note `docker system prune --volumes` has the same anonymous-only default).

findings.summary: The yellow sticky note and its red pushpin are layered on top of the "Back Up A Volume" code block, obscuring the `-C` flag in the tar command.
findings.evidence: Third code line reads `tar czf /backup/v.tgz -C /data .` but the pushpin graphic sits directly over the `C`, and the sticky note ("restore by untarring into a fresh volume") covers the lower portion of the dashed code-block area.
findings.fix: Move the sticky note (and pin) below the dashed code block's bottom border, or reduce the code block's bottom padding so the note anchors clear of the final command line.

findings.summary: The triage table maps "refused between containers" to cross-network isolation, but Docker's isolation and FORWARD rules DROP those packets, so the symptom is a timeout — contradicting the page's own rule.
findings.evidence: ["refused between containers","not on the same network"] alongside "A refusal proves the packet arrived; a timeout does not." and "timeout, not refusal" → "firewall / routing / **MTU**"
findings.fix: Re-map the row: "refused between containers" → "wrong port, or target bound to 127.0.0.1 inside its own namespace"; move "not on the same network" (DOCKER-ISOLATION DROP) under the timeout row next to firewall/routing.

findings.summary: `tcpdump -i docker0` only sees the default bridge, not the user-defined networks the rest of the handbook tells you to use.
findings.fix: Say the bridge interface is `br-<net-id>` for user-defined networks — find it with `docker network inspect -f '{{.Id}}' n` (first 12 chars) or `ip -br link`; `docker0` is only the default bridge.

findings.summary: The per-packet NAT cost claim is wrong on two counts: only the first packet of a flow traverses the nat table (the rest are translated by conntrack), and container-to-container traffic on the same bridge is never NATed.
findings.evidence: "Bridge = one veth traversal + iptables NAT per packet."
findings.fix: Reword to: "Bridge = one veth traversal + conntrack per packet; NAT chains are hit once per flow, and only for egress/published ports — same-network container traffic is not NATed."

findings.summary: A headingless list of networking anti-patterns is dropped between the storage write-path table and the networking model diagram, breaking the storage→summary flow.
findings.evidence: After the table rows "bind mount, Desktop | VM boundary — slow" comes the cross-style list "Publishing on 0.0.0.0 out of habit." / "Hardcoding container IPs — they move on restart." / "Trusting **UFW**…" / "`--link` instead of a user-defined network.", immediately followed by "4. The Model, One Line".
findings.fix: Move that cross list to page 1 beside the symptom table (networking failure modes), or give it a heading and place it with the page-2 networking cost section before "1. Storage Speed Truth".

findings.summary: The one-line networking model diagram — the anchor of the closing summary — is stranded on the trade-offs page, separated from the rest of the summary on pages 3-4.
findings.evidence: Page 2 ends with "4. The Model, One Line" and the flow "net namespace → veth pair → bridge → iptables NAT → the world", then security bullets; the other summary pieces are page 3's driver table and "5. Six Lines To Keep" and page 4's "Final Model" callout.
findings.fix: Move the model diagram to the head of the summary material on page 3, directly before the driver cheat-sheet table.

findings.summary: "Only userns-remap" is an overstatement — rootless Docker also removes the container-root = host-root equivalence.
findings.fix: Change to "Only a user-namespace mapping breaks that — `userns-remap`, or rootless Docker."

findings.summary: "The default bridge resolves nothing" is misleading: containers there still resolve external names from the host's copied /etc/resolv.conf; what they lack is container-name resolution.
findings.fix: Change to "Per-network — the default bridge resolves no container names (it just copies the host's `/etc/resolv.conf` for external lookups)."

findings.summary: The consolidated debug-order callout sits on the final page between a volume backup snippet and the DNS recap, three pages after the debugging material it orders.
findings.evidence: Page 4 sequence: lifecycle table → "6. Back Up A Volume" code → callout "Debug Order": "inspect, then 0.0.0.0?, then same network?, then firewall/MTU, then netshoot inside the target namespace." → "7. DNS In One Box".
findings.fix: Move the Debug Order callout to page 1 as the closer of the debugging section (or duplicate it there), leaving page 4 to run cleanup → backup → DNS → final model.

findings.summary: The DNS recap lands on the last page, after cleanup and backups, even though page 1's symptom table already leans on it.
findings.evidence: Page 1 table row "name not found | default bridge — no DNS"; the explanation "Resolver sits at ==127.0.0.11== on user-defined networks." / "Per-network — the default bridge resolves **nothing**." appears only in page 4's "7. DNS In One Box".
findings.fix: Move the DNS box to page 3 with the driver cheat sheet (networking recap together), or place it on page 1 adjacent to the symptom table so the "no DNS" row is immediately explained.
